sources.title: Theoretical Analysis of the Radio Map Estimation Problem
sources.actual_reading: local theory.txt lines 59-115 abstract/introduction, 127-169 formulation and nonstationarity footnote, 708-716 conclusions/limitations; keyword matches inspected; proofs and remaining sections not fully read
takeaways: Power-map spatial variability depends on source proximity; near sources require denser measurements in the analyzed setting.
The main reconstruction theory assumes free-space propagation and stationary power; the formulation explicitly cautions that practical nonstationary measurements need a common short timescale.
The conclusion leaves noise and reflection/refraction/absorption/diffraction to further analysis.
sources.use: Motivates testing bounded source center/scale changes without treating coarse dictionary geometry or fit loss as reliable ahead-of-route reconstruction.
limitations: Does not establish identifiability of Gaussian equivalent-source parameters from a single noisy moving trajectory.
Does not justify the project-specific 40m/sqrt(2) refinement bounds.
Does not transfer static free-space guarantees to the project dynamic obstructed simulator.
No LLM organization or UAV decision gain is established by this paper.
